title: ShopMind — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Specimen Plate world (your grounded candidate #7). Keep it, take the pick or a challenger, go category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: Specimen Plate
options.lineage: museum & herbarium cataloging sheets — plate, label block, family color
options.thesis: Every product is a catalogued specimen: a plate, a fixed label block, one assigned hue per family.
options.viewport: Ink rail navigation on cool archival paper; the catalog grid reads as specimen plates — each cell a plate area over a fixed caption block (SKU, family, stock) ruled in its family hue; the header names the first–last entry currently in view.
options.risk: Reads as a craft-shop template if the label blocks ever lose their data discipline.

raised.raise: Guide words recomputed live: the list header always names the first and last specimen in view.
One fixed color language with a printed legend: no hue appears anywhere unless the legend already says what it means.
Whole-cell reflow: the roster is ranked and finite, and cells reflow in whole units, never stretched.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Numbers are mechanical truth: every live figure visibly flipped into its current position.
options.viewport: A dark instrument rail across the top with live counters (open quotes, reserved stock); working rows on paper beneath; every number that changed in the last turn shows its flip.
options.risk: Also the direction live-data demos often land on; the flip is novelty if the numbers aren’t genuinely live.

options.label: Data-matics Field
options.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda data art — barcodes, lattices, pure black and white
options.thesis: The shop as a strobing data field; products are columns of exact figures.
options.viewport: Barcode lattice header; dense monospace product columns; selection pulls one column into focus, the field dims.
options.case: Holds the audience axis — engineers know it by heart; loses product clarity because pure B&W refuses the semantic color a store needs for stock and payment state.
options.risk: Zero-color law forces stock/paid/failed states into typography alone.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.lineage: Peter Saville’s Factory Records sleeve system — fac numbers, matte black
options.thesis: Everything is a catalog entry; names are encoded as strips of color blocks you decode once.
options.viewport: Products numbered fac-style in strict sequence; a hue strip encodes each category, hovering decodes it to text; one plot owns the field.
options.case: Catalog-number discipline fuses directly onto SKUs; loses on scanability — its 'nothing labeled twice' law fights an operating screen.
options.risk: Encoded labels hide meaning behind hover on screens built for glancing.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.lineage: modern consumer app surfaces — soft cards, one action color
options.thesis: Comfortable cards, human-sounding labels, and color reserved strictly for what you can press.
options.viewport: Single scrolling column of roomy cards; the only saturated hue on screen is always an actionable control; thumb-reachable bar persists.
options.case: Wins outright on task clarity for demo shoppers; loses audience identification — it is every SaaS demo your reviewers have seen.
options.risk: Crafted generic: nothing here says ShopMind.

options.label: Lexicon Spread
options.case: Loses both axes: cream-and-serif broadsheet is the calibration rut, and newspaper columns on a working screen are costume.
options.kept: Guide words recomputed from the visible span — now a named raise on the assigned card.

options.label: Orienteering Map
materials: isom inks with strict assigned meaning
options.case: Runners know it, engineers don’t; a terrain layer under a product grid reads as costume on an operating surface.
options.kept: Legend-first color discipline — every hue has one assigned meaning — now a named raise on the assigned card.

options.label: Mascot Roster
options.case: Wrong register: a cute pastel roster misrepresents electronics craft; loses both axes.
options.kept: Ranked, finite roster with whole-cell reflow — now a named raise on the assigned card.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The electronics storefront reviewers expect, executed at impeccable craft.
canonCard.viewport: Header search, filter rail, product cards with hover lift, cart drawer, checkout — all convention, all polished.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every competitor by design.
